rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
**Heat Capacity Definition:** Heat capacity $C = \Delta Q/\Delta T$ is the heat required to raise temperature by 1 K. Specific heat capacity $c = C/m$ is per unit mass (J/kg·K).…
**Phase Change Latent Heat:** During phase change (melting, boiling), temperature is constant while heat is absorbed/released as latent heat: $Q = mL$.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Calorimetry Principle:** In an isolated system, heat lost by hot bodies = heat gained by cold bodies. This assumes no heat loss to surroundings and no phase changes unless accounted for. The final equilibrium temperature is found by equating $m_1 c_1 (T_f - T_1) = m_2 c_2 (T_2 - T_f)$.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Heat Capacity Definition:** Heat capacity $C = \Delta Q/\Delta T$ is the heat required to raise temperature by 1 K. Specific heat capacity $c = C/m$ is per unit mass (J/kg·K). Molar heat capacity $C_m = C/n$ is per mole (J/mol·K).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Phase Change Latent Heat:** During phase change (melting, boiling), temperature is constant while heat is absorbed/released as latent heat: $Q = mL$. Latent heat of fusion $L_f$ (solid↔liquid) and vaporization $L_v$ (liquid↔gas) are material properties.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: **Calorimetry Principle:** In an isolated system, heat lost by hot bodies = heat gained by cold bodies. This assumes no heat loss to surroundings and no phase changes unless accounted for. The final equilibrium temperature is found by equating $m_1 c_1 (T_f - T_1) = m_2 c_2 (T_2 - T_f)$.
